correctness.rationale: For arbitrary full-row-rank 2-by-n gradient, the left polar SPD factor A and row-isometry O give G_1=(A-(tr A/tr H)H)O. The symmetric bracket is trace-free and its square is scalar I_2, so G_1G_1^T is scalar I_2. At every subsequent nonzero gradient nuclear norm times polar equals 2G and the update becomes ordinary GD with effective step 2/tr H. The trace-free C=I-2H/tr H squares to rho^2I_2. All boundaries, termination and rank-one stratum are explicitly proved; 648 exact rational full-rank and 48 rank-one checks were executed, along with 300 direct numerical SVD checks.

value.rationale: The two-row finite identification theorem rigorously explains an unexpected one-step perfect gradient conditioning phenomenon for arbitrary dense, noncommuting full-rank initial matrices and exactly identifies the entire thereafter-linear optimizer orbit. It determines the precise asymptotic rate and a genuine rank-dependent discontinuity, directly addressing the motivating literature gap that general polar-gradient directional rates are not known in closed form. No additional larger-dimension theorem is needed to make this natural complete two-row classification informative.
